results.reason: Issue 3 flags §13.2: Supplier may assign without consent or notice, including to a competitor, while Customer assignment needs consent. It explains the risk to supply continuity and confidential specs (§7.1, §8.2) and proposes mutual consent with a competitor carve-out.

Issue 1 flags §13.3: Supplier consent is required for a change of control, with a termination right. It ties this to the pending sale and recommends deletion, narrowing to competitors with a reasonableness standard, or a consent/waiver before signing or closing.

Issue 4 flags Order Form §2.2: automatic three-year renewals with a 30-day notice window. It explains the lock-in risk and recommends a longer window, a shorter renewal term, or renewal by mutual agreement.

Issue 2 flags the §9.3 carve-out of Customer's §10.1 indemnity from the cap. It notes unlimited Customer exposure while Supplier stays capped, and recommends deleting the carve-out or making it mutual with a separate cap.
The memo correctly states the 12-month fees cap (§9.1), Delaware law (§12.1), and a three-year Initial Term from March 1, 2026.
The memo states the §1.3 order of precedence and analyzes the renewal provision as a gap rather than a conflict, so precedence does not override it.
A priority table ranks change of control and the uncapped indemnity as High and first, ahead of the lesser issues.
Each issue follows a Where / What it says / Why it matters / Recommended fix structure with proposed language. The memo ends with an open questions and business decisions section.
The Specifications Schedule is expressly found to raise no issue. No external statutes or cases are cited, and no invented issues are flagged as significant.
